translations.text: Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who in his great mercy has begotten us again into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
into an inheritance that is incorruptible, undefiled and unfading, kept in the heavens for you,
who are guarded by the power of God through faith for the salvation that is prepared to be revealed in the last time.
In this you now rejoice, even though for a little while, if it must be so, you have been grieved by many kinds of trials,
so that the testing of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes and than tested silver, may be found to result in praise, glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
You did not know him, yet you love him; you do not see him now, yet you believe in him; and you rejoice with a joy that cannot be put into words and with glory.
And at the end of your faith you will receive the salvation of your souls.
The prophets who prophesied about the grace that was to come to you searched and inquired carefully about this salvation,
asking when, or at what time, the Spirit of Christ within them was making it known, when it testified in advance about the sufferings of Christ and his glories that would come after them.

It was revealed to them that they were serving it not for themselves but for you. It has now been announced to you by your evangelists through the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, and the angels long to look into it.
Therefore gird up the loins of your minds, be watchful, and set your hope fully on the grace that is coming to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
As children of obedience, do not shape yourselves after the desires you had before, in your ignorance,
but just as the one who called you is holy, you also must be holy in all your conduct.
For it is written: "Be holy, for I am holy."
And if you call on him as Father, who judges each person's works without partiality, live out the time of your sojourning in fear.
Know that you were not redeemed with perishable gold or silver from the empty way of life handed down to you by your fathers,
but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot.
He was known in advance, before the creation of the world, and was revealed in the last times for your sake.
Through him you believe in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith may be with God.
Purify your souls by obedience to the truth. Be sincere and without hypocrisy, from the heart, for the sake of love for the brothers, and love one another earnestly.
For you have been born again, not from perishable seed but from imperishable seed, through the word of God, which is eternal.
For all flesh is grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the grass. The grass has withered, and its flower has fallen away.
But the word of the Lord stands and remains forever.
They stumble at the word through disobedience, and that is what they were appointed to.
But you are a chosen light [?], a royal priesthood, a holy seed, a people acquired as God's own, so that you may proclaim the virtues of him who called you out of darkness into his light,
You who once were not a people of God, but now are the people of God; who once had not received mercy, but now have received mercy.
Beloved, I beseech you, as strangers and sojourners, keep away from fleshly desires, which wage war against the soul.
Keep your conduct among the gentiles good, so that in the very thing for which they speak evil of you as evildoers, they may observe [?] your good works and glorify God on the day of visitation.
[?] for the doers [of evil], and for the praise of those who do good,
for such is the will of God for those who do good, and to stop the mouths of foolish men in their ignorance;
as free people, and not having that freedom of yours as a covering for wickedness, but as servants of God.
Honour everyone, love the brothers, fear God, honour the king.
Servants, submit in all things to your own masters, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the harsh.
For this is grace from God: if, for the sake of a good conscience, we endure sorrow when we are made to suffer unjustly.
What is better, if we sin and are beaten and endure it? But if we do good and suffer and endure it, this is grace from God.
For this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you and left you a written example, so that you may follow in his footsteps;
he who committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth;
who was reviled and reviled no one, suffered and harmed no one, and was handed over to the judge unjustly;
who himself bore our sins in his flesh upon the tree, so that we may be delivered from sin and live in righteousness; by his wounds we were healed.
For we were like sheep gone astray, but now we have turned back to the Shepherd and Teacher of our souls.
For in this way once the holy women also, who hoped in the Lord, adorned themselves and were submissive to their own husbands,
as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord; whose [children] you have become, doing good and not being afraid of any terror.
Husbands, likewise, live with them with forbearance, as with the weaker vessel, giving honour to the women as co-heirs of the grace of life, so that you do not hinder your prayer.
It is better, if the will of God should so please, that you suffer while doing good than while doing evil.
For Christ also suffered once for our sins, so that he might bring us to God; he died in the flesh and was made alive in the spirit,
in which he went and preached to the spirits in prison,
who were once disobedient, when the long-suffering of God waited in the days of Noah, during the preparation of the ark, in which a few, that is, eight souls, were saved from the water.
In the likeness of this, baptism now saves you also: not the removal of filth from the flesh, but a mind pleasing to God, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
who is at the right hand of God, who ascended into heaven, and angels, authorities and powers were made subject to him.
Purify yourselves and be watchful for prayer.
Above all, keep your love for one another fervent, for love covers a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
As each one has received a gift from God, so serve one another with it, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.
Whoever speaks, let it be as the words of God; whoever serves, let it be as from the strength that God supplies, so that in all things God may be glorified.
Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal that is taking place among you to test you, as though something strange were happening to you.
But inasmuch as you share [?]
[?] God in that name.
For the time has come for judgment to begin first with the house of God; and if it begins first with us, what will be the end of those who disobey the gospel of God?
And if the righteous is scarcely saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?
Therefore let those who suffer according to the will of God entrust their souls to the Lord, the Creator of faith, by doing good.
I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a fellow witness of the sufferings of Christ, and a sharer in the glory that is to be revealed: shepherd the flock of God that is among you.
Watch over it not under compulsion but as God would have it, not for shameful gain but eagerly.
Do not lord it over the priests, but be examples to the flock.
so that when the Chief Shepherd appears you may receive the unfading crown of righteousness.
